proposals.sourceEvidence: vā́la m. 'hair of tail, tail, hair' TS., vālaka- m. 'tail of horse or elephant' lex. [~ vā́ra-¹] Pa. Pk. vāla- m. 'hair' (Pa. also 'hair of tail'), Gy. eur. bal m., arm. valis, pal. wal, wáli; Ḍ. bāli f. 'cord, string (consisting of goat's hair attached to the weaving bow to which ends of warp threads are fastened)'; Dm. iž-bấli 'eyebrow'; Tir. bālē m. 'hair'; Paš. wāl 'a hair'; Bshk. Tor. bāl 'hair', Kand. bālə, Mai bāla, Phal. bōla, būla, °lu, Sh.gil. bālṷ, pl. °le̯ m., koh. bālŭ m., pales. bāl, °lo; K. wāl m. 'hair of head, down of body'; S. vāru m. 'hair', L. vāl m. (khet. akkhin de vāl 'eyelashes'), P. vāl, bāl m., WPah.bhal. bā m., cam. bāḷ, Ku. bāl, gng. bāw, N. bāl; A. B. bāl 'pubic hair', Or. bāḷa; Bhoj. bār 'hair', H. bāl m., G. vāḷ m; Si. val-a 'hair, esp. hair of tail'. *vālaguccha-, *vālapāśī-, *vālavījana-, vālāgra-; *nivāla-, *jātavāla-, *barkaravāla-, *mūrdhavāla-, *śirōvāla-; — pravāla-¹? Addenda: vā́la-: WPah.kṭg. bāḷ m.pl. 'hair', J. bā'l m., Garh. bāḷ. †*ārkavāla-, †*karṇavāla-, †*skandhavāla-.

proposals.evidence: Compare Shina mŭkh and Sauji mukhá. Turner discusses these under mukhya but explicitly prefers mukha with expressive doubling; keep that uncertainty in the proposed parent.
proposals.sourceEvidence: múkha n. 'mouth, face' RV., 'entrance' MBh. Pa. mukha- m.; Aś.shah. man. gir. mukhato, kāl. dh. jau. °te 'by word of mouth'; Pk. muha- n. 'mouth, face', Gy. gr. hung. muy m., boh. muy, span. muí, wel. mūī f., arm. muc̦, pal. mu', mi', pers. mu; Tir. mū 'face'; Woṭ. mū m. 'face, sight'; Kho. mux 'face'; Tor. mū 'mouth', Mai. mũ; K. in cmpds. mu-ganḍ m. 'cheek, upper jaw', mū-kāla 'having one's face blackened', rām. mūī˜, pog. mūī, ḍoḍ. mū̃h 'mouth'; S. mũhũ m. 'face, mouth, opening'; L. mũh m. 'face', awāṇ. mū̃ with descending tone, mult. mũhã m. 'head of a canal'; P. mū̃h m. 'face, mouth', mū̃hā̃ m. 'head of a canal'; WPah.śeu. mũ̀ 'mouth,' cur. mū̃h; A. muh 'face', in cmpds. -muwā 'facing'; B. mu 'face'; Or. muhã 'face, mouth, head, person'; Bi. mũh 'opening or hole (in a stove for stoking, in a handmill for filling, in a grainstore for withdrawing)'; Mth. Bhoj. mũh 'mouth, face', Aw.lakh. muh, H. muh, mũh m.; OG. muha, G. mɔ̃h n. 'mouth', Si. muya, muva. — Ext. -l- or -ll-: Pk. muhala-, muhulla- n. 'mouth, face'; S. muhuro m. 'face' (or < mukhará-); Ku. do-maulo 'confluence of two streams'; Si. muhul, muhuna, mūṇa 'face' H. Smith JA 1950, 179.; — -ḍ-: S. muhaṛo m. 'front, van'; Bi. (Shahabad) mohṛā 'feeding channel of handmill'. — Forms poss. with expressive -kkh-: see múkhya-. — X gōcchā- s.v. *mucchā-. mukhará-, múkhya-, maukhya-; *mukhakāṣṭha-, *mukhaghāṭā-, mukhacandra-, *mukhajāla-, *mukhanātha-, mukhatuṇḍaka-, *mukhatuttikā-, *mukhadhara-, mukhaśuddhi-, *mukhahāra-, mukhāgra-, *mukhāñcala-, *mukhānta-, *mukhāyana-; amukhá-, abhimukhá-, āmukha-, unmukha-, *nirmukha-; adhōmukha-, ūrdhvamukha-, kālamukha-, gṓmukha-, caturmukha-, *paścamukha-, valīmukha-, śilīmukha-, saṁmukhá-, *sāṁmukha-, sumukha-. Addenda: múkha-: WPah.kṭg. (kc.) mū̃ (with high level tone) m. (obl. -a) 'mouth, face'; OMarw. muhaṛaü 'face'. †*agramukha-, †*agrāmukha-.

proposals.evidence: Specific *nastī subsection: Shina Jijel nöti nose, with the final i; distinguish nastaka forms with masculine -o.
proposals.sourceEvidence: nasta m. 'nose' lex. 2. nastaka- m. 'septum of nose, hole bored through it in oxen' MBh. 3. *nastī-. 4. *nastu-. 5. nastā- f. 'hole bored in septum of nose' lex. 6. *nastya-. [A stem *nast- perh. in nastás 'from or into the nose' ŚBr. and in Ir. *nāstĭ̄ > Par. nēšt 'nose' IIFL i 277, poss. also in *nakka- if < *nastka-] 1. Paš.lauṛ. nāst, nās m., ar. nōəst, gul. nūst, chil. nāst 'nose'; L. nath m. 'nose ring'; M. nāth m. 'nose string'; — orig. gender unknown: Tir. nΛst 'nose', Kal. urt. nāst; Kho. nast 'in front of' (< *nāsta- ?); Tor. nat 'nostril', natkōl 'nose', Sh.pales. nΛtkṓl (+?); Mai. nathūr 'nose'; Ku. nāthūr, °thuro 'bleeding from nose' (+?); K. nath- 'nose' (in nath-wöjᷴ f. 'nose ring'), kash. nasth, pog. nāht. 2. Kand. natho 'nose', Sh.koh. pales. nΛtho, gil. (Lor.) natho, (T. G. Bailey) natŭ m., koh. notŭ, gur. nōttŭ m. 3. Woṭ. nyet f. 'nose'; Phal. nā̆st f. 'nose', nasti-ṣṓṛa 'nostril'; Sh.jij. nöˊti 'nose'. 4. Pa. natthu- f. 'nose'. 5. Pk. ṇatthā- f. 'nose string'; S. natha f. 'nose ring, rope through nose of ox or camel'; L. natth f. 'nosering'; P. natth f. 'nose string'; N. nāth 'rope through bullock's nose', Bi. nāth; Mth. nāth 'nose ring', Bhoj. nathunī; Aw.lakh. nāth 'nose rope', H. G. nāth f.; H. nathiyā f. 'nose ring'; — ext. -ḍa-: N. nāthri 'nostrils', nāthro 'eye of a needle'. — With a (← NW?): Ku. nath f., nathuli f., °lo m. 'nose ring for women', B. nath, Or. natha, notha, G. M. nath f. — Verbal deriv.: Pk. ṇatthaṇa- n. 'boring the nose'; S. nathaṇu 'to pierce the nose', L. natthaṇ, P. natthṇā, N. nāthnu, H. nāthnā (whence intr. nathnā 'to have the nose bored'), G. nāthvũ, M. nāthṇẽ. 6. Niṅg. nečū́ 'nose', Shum. načū; — Kal.rumb. nā́čur. Addenda: nasta-. 5. nastā-: S.kcch. nath f. 'nose ring, nose rope'; WPah.kṭg. nəkthv́ṇi f. 'nostril' (metath. *nath + kvṇe < kōṇa- Him.I 168), nəkthóḷi f. 'nostril'; J. nakthrō f. 'bleeding from the nostrils' (similarly metath. *nathkōl-, °kor).

'belly', L. ḍhiḍḍh m., awāṇ. ḍhiḍ, P. ḍhiḍḍ(h) m., ḍhiḍḍī f.; Mth. ḍhīṛhā 'gravid womb'; H. ḍhīṛh 'id.', ḍhīḍhā m. 'back'. 2. S. ḍ̠iḍhu m. 'belly', °ḍho m. 'id., centre piece of a paper kite'. 3. proposals.evidence: Compare Shina Jijel tΛl palm and Kohistani tălī sole/palm. The feminine extensions are explicitly included under tala.
proposals.sourceEvidence: tala n. 'base, bottom' Mn., 'surface, flat roof' MBh., (in cmpd. with 'hand' or 'foot', later alone) 'palm, sole' n. (later m.) MBh. 2. *talla-² (< *talya- ?). [Cf. *tara-³?] 1. Pa. Pk. tala- n. 'level, ground, surface, bottom, palm, sole'; Ḍ. tΛl m. 'ceiling', Λc̣hi-tΛl 'eyelid'; Wg. tōl 'cultivated field', Kt. tul; Dm. tal 'ceiling'; Paš.lauṛ. dar. tāl, kuṛ. tōl 'roof, ceiling'; Shum. tal 'ceiling'; Sh. gil. tăl m. 'sole of foot', tal m. 'ceiling (under roof)', koh. gur. tăl m. 'id.', jij. tΛl 'palm'; K. tala m. 'bottom'; S. taru m. 'surface, floor, bottom (of pond &c.)', taro m. 'sole of shoe, bottom (in general), dregs'; P. talā m. 'sole of shoe'; WPah.bhad. bhal. tal n. 'ground, floor of a house'; Ku. talo 'base'; N. talo 'storey'; A. tal, talā 'flat surface, bottom'; B. tal 'bottom, floor, sole, palm', talā 'bottom, groundwork'; Or. taḷa 'flat surface, bottom, sole, palm', taḷā 'leather glove worn by archers'; Mth. tal 'surface, bottom, palm'; H. talā, tarā m. 'bottom'; OMarw. talaü m. 'bottom', talā-su 'from below'; G. taḷ, taḷũ n. 'flat surface, bottom, sole'; M. taḷ m. 'bottom', n. 'central board in a potter's wheel'; Si. talaya 'surface, bottom, palm, blade of weapon' (alla 'palm' < at-tala, palla 'sole' < patla < pa-tala). — As adv. and postp.: Gy. eur. tel, tele 'under', telal 'from under' (< MIA. *talādo); Mai. tal 'on'; K. tal, talⁱ 'beneath', tala 'from below'; L. talē 'below', WPah.cur. taḷē; Ku. tali 'down, under'; N. tala 'below', A. B. tale, Or. taḷe, Bhoj. tar, OAw. tara, H. tar, tare, tale, OMarw. talaï, G. taḷε. — Feminines in -ī-, -ikā-: Pk. taligā-, °iyā- f. 'shoe'; Bshk. til 'palm'; Tor. tel f. 'roof'; Mai. talī 'earth' NTS xviii 124; Phal. talī́ 'sole, fireplace'; Sh.koh. tălī 'sole, palm', gil. (Lor.) tΛli 'platform'; S. tarī, tirī f. 'palm, sole'; L. tal f. 'bottom', talī f. proposals.evidence: Shina paṣ wool directly matches. Turner explicitly allows an Iranian loan origin for these northwestern wool words, so inherited pakṣman remains provisional, with Persian pašm as an alternative.
proposals.sourceEvidence: pákṣman n. (sg. and pl.) 'eyelashes' TS., 'hair of a deer, filament of a flower' Śiś., 'petal of a flower' Kād., 'a thin thread' lex. Forms, esp. of the North-west, with -ṣp-, -ṣ-, -m(b)h- and meaning 'wool', may with G. Morgenstierne BSOS viii 668, though not certainly, be ← Ir., cf. Pers. pašm 'wool'. — Pa. pakhuma-, pamha- n. (X bhavā̃ s.v. bhrū́-) 'eyelashes', phamb(h) f. 'fine kind of Tibetan wool'; WPah.bhal. bimphṇi f. 'eyelash'; Bi. pambhī, (W) pā̃bhī, pā̃kī, (Patna) pakhnī 'fine chaff blown away in winnowing of winter crop'; Mth. papᵃnī 'eyelash'; Bhoj. pāmhī 'little whisker'; H. papnī f. proposals.evidence: Shina, Sauji and Palula ma I explicitly continue the old oblique ma-base used nominatively, not aham.
proposals.sourceEvidence: ma base of singular oblique cases of 1st person pronoun: acc. mā́m, inst. máyā, dat. máhyam, gen. máma, encl. mē. Pa. maṁ, mayā, mayhaṁ, mama; Aś. acc. maṁ, inst. mayā, gen. shah. man. maa, gir. kāl. dh. mama; NiDoc. gen. dat. mama, mahi; Pk. acc. maṁ, mamaṁ, inst. maē, gen. mama, majjhaṁ, Ap. inst. maï˜. — Except in some peripheral NIA. languages a form based for the most part on Pk. inst. maē (with substitution of nominal inst. ending -eṁ < -ēna) has taken the place of old nominative ahám; Gy. eur. me 'I', pal. ắma; Chil. Gau. Sv. Phal. Sh. ma (but Phal. inst. mē, mī), S.srk. mā̃, mū̃; L. maĩ, mε῀ nom. and inst., P. maĩ, WPah.jaun. mē̃ (nom. also hāũ, aũ); Garh. maĩ, mĩ (inst. maĩn), Ku. maĩ, mī (inst. maĩle), N. ma, emph. maĩ (inst. maile), A. maï, B. (vulgar) mui, Or. mu, mũ; OAw. maïṁ nom. and inst.; H. maĩ (inst. maĩne), OMarw. mẽ, M. mī˜, mī. — Other forms: Pr. əm gen.; Tir. masi 'to me'; Kho. ma acc. and gen.; Tor. Sv. mī gen.; K. mĕ dat. inst. abl.; S. encl. -mi 'of, to, by me' < mē, L. encl. -m; WPah.bhad. maĩ inst. (aũ nom.), G. mε῀; Si. mama nom.; — H. mujh obl.; OG. majha dat., M. maj̈ obl., māj̈hā 'my', Ko. majjo. — The genitive is replaced by a declinable adjective with various suffixes: Gaw. mōna, Tir. myāna, K. myônᵘ; — Gy. gr. minro, SEeur. moi̦ó m., mei̦í f., L. maĩḍā, maiḍā; — Ap. mahāriya-, mēra-, WP. mε῀rā, P. merā, WPah. jaun. Garh. Ku. N. mero, A. mohora, mora, Or. mohara, OAw. moraü, H. merā, OMarw. meraü, OG. māharaü, G. mārũ. — See ahám, māmaká-. MAṀH 'give': máhas-². Addenda: ma-: Kho. ma 'me' obl. BKhoT 70; WPah.kṭg. mũ 'I'; Md. ma 'I, me' (gen. ma-ge, dat. mařař). †mámat. †makkaṇa- see matkuṇa-².

proposals.evidence: Exact Shina and Palula tu and Torwali tū; the inherited singular pronoun continues tuvam.
proposals.sourceEvidence: tuvám (metr.), tvám 'thou'. 2. Acc. tuvā́m (metr.), tvā́m. 3. Inst. tvā́ 4. Gen. táva. 5. Dat. túbhya(m) RV. 1. Nom.: Pa. tuvaṁ, tvaṁ, NiDoc. tu, tuo, Pk. tumaṁ, tuṁ, taṁ, Gy. eur. tu, pal. ắtu, Ḍ. tu, Ash. tū, Wg. tu, tṳ̄, Pr. iyū, Dm. tu, Tir. tu, tə, ta, Paš. Niṅg. Shum. Gaw. tu, Kal. tū̆, tüi, Kho. tu, Bshk. Tor. Mai. tū, Sv. Phal. Sh. tu, K.rām. pog. kash. tu, S. tū̃, L. P. tũ, WPah.bhad. bhal. pāḍ. paṅ. cur. tū, khaś. tũ, Ku. tū, N. tã, B. Or. Bhoj. tu, OAw. tūṁ, H. OMarw. tū, tū̃, M. tū̃, Ko. tū. — Not all forms come directly < tuvám, e.g. NiDoc. tuo; Pk. tuhaṁ after ahám, Ap. tuhu with -hu from ehu 'this' L. A. Schwarzschild JAOS 80, 15, OA. tuhã; G. tū̃ < OG. taüṁ after haüṁ 'I' Dave GujLg 145. 2. Acc.: Pa. taṁ, Pk. tuvaṁ, tumaṁ, tuṁ, taṁ, Wg. tū. 3. Inst.: Dm. -p as suffix of 2nd sg. pret. (extended to aor.) e.g. kurōp orig. 'it was done by thee' NTS xii 141: cf. Ap. paï˜ < *tvayēna. 4. Gen.: Pa. NiDoc. Pk. tava, Dm. Gaw. tō, B. to ODBL 817, Or. to (perh. rather < toho); — as acc.: Shum. Sh.pales. tō; — as nom.; — Si. tō GS 124 (or < Pk. tuha or even < tuvám). 5. Dat.: Pk. tubbhaṁ, °bha. — Replaced by Pa. tuyhaṁ after máhyam s.v. ma-, Pk. tujjhā̆ (as gen. abl.), A. tazu (gen.), H. tujh (gen. obl.), G. poet. tuja 'thine', M. tuj̈hā; — < contracted *tjjha-: Bshk. čhā̃ 'thine' AO. xviii 231, Tor. čhī, K. ċ- (nom. ċᵃh, acc. dat. ċĕ, inst. ċe, possessive adj. cyônᵘ). — *tuddha- (cf. Ap. tudhra) as gen. obl. in L.poṭh. tuddh and poss. in Gy. eur. tut (for *thud with t- after nom. tu). — Possessive adj. formed with -ra- or -kā̆ra- or -kēra-: Ap. tuhara-, B. Or. tora; — P. H. terā, Ku. N. tero; — G. tārɔ; — Gy. eur. tiro, arm. terav in face of SEeur. toi̦ó, tii̦í is to be connected rather with L. teḍā. Addenda: tuvám: Kho. tu 'thou', obl. ta, dat. tat BKhoT 73, WPah.kṭg. (kc.) tū, tu, poet. tue pl. 'you'; Garh. tu, A. tui, Md. ta.

proposals.evidence: Compare Shina Gurez ăsõ and Sauji asō; the asmad base accounts for the plural first-person forms. Preserve inclusive/exclusive elicitation records independently.
proposals.sourceEvidence: asmad base of obl. cases plur. of 1st pers. pronoun asmā́n, asmā́bhiḥ, asmábhyam, asmā́kam, asmā́su, dat. loc. asmḗ. Pa. nom. acc. amhē (-ē after other pronouns), gen. amhākaṁ, inst. amhēhi; Aś. dh. acc. aphe, gen. aphākaṁ, loc. aphesu; NiDoc. gen. asmakaṁ, inst. asmehi; Pk. nom. acc. amhē, gen. amhāṇaṁ, inst. amhēhiṁ. The Kaf. and Dard. forms are discussed in detail by Morgenstierne IL v 357 ff.: Ash. ima 'we', Kt. emo, Wg. amī́, Pr. asẽ; Dm. obl. amâ, mâ; Tir. mā 'we', Paš. hamā́, Shum. ābə (< *ambhē), gen. amana (←Paš.); Woṭ. mā acc. pl.; Gaw. amō̃ 'we'; Kal. dir. ābi, obl. hamā; Kho. dir. and obl. ispa; Tor. nom. mō, inst. mahī, gen. amun, mun; Mai. gen. zā̃, Chil. azā̃, Gau. asā̃, Phal. asī, Sh. ăsĕi, gur. ăsō̃. In the remaining languages the declension rests mainly on three MIA. forms: — *asmē, *asmānaṁ, *asmēhi with a tendency in the mod. stage for the successors of *asmē to be replaced by the inst. (as often in the case of 1st pers. sg. see ahám): Gy. eur. ame, pal. ắme, as. emi; Ḍ. Λmέ, gen. ama; K. ȧsⁱ, gen. sônᵘ, S. asī˜ (< *asmēhiṁ), obl. asā̃; L. asã: asã; P. asī˜: asā̃; WPah. as: asan ~ jaun. ām; OB. ambhe, āmhe (Chatterji ODBL 809), āmi: āmā; Or. āmbhe, āme, ami: āmbha; Mth. Bhoj. Aw. H. dir. and obl. ham; OG. āma, mod. ame, M. āmhī, Ko. āmī (these three orig. inst.); Si. äp < apphe, apa < apphākaṁ (Geiger EGS 8 wrongly < ātmán-). asmā́ka-. Addenda: asmad-: Kho. ispā́ 'we' BKhoT 68, S.kcch. asī˜ dir. 'we', obl. asā̃-, Garh. ham dir. and obl., A. āmi.

proposals.sourceEvidence: nikaṭam, °ṭē, °ṭāt adv. 'near' R. [Despite EWA ii 158 derivation with P. Tedesco JAOS 65, 161 f. from nikr̥ṣṭa- is phonet. impossible, and Mu. origin with F. B. J. Kuiper Debrunner-Festschrift 247 unlikely. Derived from nikr̥ta- adverbially preserving the mng. '*put at' (semant. cf. saṁnihita- 'near') afterwards replaced by 'put down, humbled' (J.C.W.)] Pa. nikaṭa- 'near', Pk. ṇiaḍa-, ṇiala-, ṇiaḍia-, Dm. nyεiŕ, nyäyᵃ, Paš.kuṛ. nyōṛṓ, Gaw. nyāṛɔ, Bshk. nī́er Tor. niō, Sv. nyeṛo, Phal. nihā́ṛa, K. adj. nyūrᵘ, f.nīrᷴ, adv. nēri (< nikaṭē), rām. nēṛē, pog. nēṛi, kash. niōṛᵘ, L. neṛe; P. neṛā m. 'vicinity', neṛe 'near'; WPah.bhad. nēṛō, paṅ. cur. nīṛ; Ku. neṛo adj., N. nira adv., OB. niaḍi, B. niyaṛ, Or. niāṛa, Mth. Bhoj. niyar, OAw. niyara, lakh. nērē, H. neṛe, nīṛe, nīre, G. neṛε. naikaṭya-. Addenda: nikaṭam: WPah.kṭg. néḍḍhi, neḍi 'near' adv., Wkc. nεṛu, J. neṛē, kiũth. nĕūṛē (u < r̥ in nikr̥ta- ?).

proposals.evidence: Compare Palula krin- and Shina krin- sell, explicitly listed by Turner under krīṇāti buy. Ushojo kirn- has vowel metathesis relative to krin-; the elicited future ending is local inflection, and the metathesis remains qualified.
proposals.sourceEvidence: krīṇā́ti 'buys' RV. [In NIA. replaced by √grabh in NW, W, SW, and by √labh in Centre, P. Tedesco JAOS 43, 377. — √krī] Pa. kiṇāti, NiDoc. krinita 'bought', Pk. kīṇaï, kiṇ°, kiriṇ° (← Sk. or NWPk.); Gy. pal. kúnăr 'sells', eur. kin- 'to buy'; Kho. krenik, pp. kreniru 'to buy'; Phal. krin- 'to sell', Sh. gil. (Lor.) krinoiki, imper. krin, gur. krĭnyōnṷ, K. kᵃnun; N. kinnu 'to buy', A. kiniba, B. kinā, Or. kiṇibā, Bi. kīnab, Mth. kīnab, kin°, Bhoj. kinal, H. kīnnā, kin°, OSi. inscr. kiṇiya absol., caus. keṇavi.
